description: EXPLORATORY. Closes qou-768r route 3's stated Delta = 2 residual by DIRECT COMPUTATION: mubar vanishes on EVERY triple of the derived carrier, in both crossing-resolution branches, across 7 isotopes and all three indeterminacy classes. Uses Milnor's ORIGINAL definition -- the degree-2 Magnus coefficient of the k-th longitude -- which for a braid closure is read straight off the word and needs NO Seifert surface. That corrects two of my own claims from this session: that no held work supplies the Magnus route (Mellor-Melvin does), and then that Seifert surfaces for the torus-knot components were the obstacle (they are one route, not the route). The BORROMEAN RINGS are computed by the same code path and asserted NONZERO as a positive control -- without it an all-zero result is indistinguishable from a broken implementation. Scope (a) on the carrier as given; the Borromean control is itself a counterexample to any reading that Milnor invariants vanish generally. Nothing wired.

what_was_open.route_3_closed: Delta = 0 (min-span) triples, by a STRUCTURAL argument: no shared summand => split sublink => mubar = 0
what_was_open.the_residual: Delta = 2 triples -- touching a linked pair, one bit of mubar surviving. No mubar VALUE had ever been computed in this corpus.
what_was_open.correction_1: my literature ledger and qou-768r both said no held work supplies the Magnus-longitude route. Mellor-Melvin (library/0110001v3/) gives the general mod-delta formula. The OTHER held source (arxiv-1101.3374v1) really is restricted to vanishing pairwise linking, which is why the claim read plausible.
what_was_open.correction_2: having found that, I named SEIFERT SURFACES as the obstacle -- the components are (2,odd)-torus knots so their surfaces are not discs. Also wrong, and the more useful error: Milnor's original longitude definition needs no surface, and a braid closure hands the longitude over directly.

positive_controls.why: a null result is worth exactly as much as its calibration, and an all-zero first run is when a bug is most likely

borromean_rings.reading: textbook mubar_123 = +/-1; detected, so a genuine nonzero is visible

convention.over_strand: sigma_i sends the strand at position i OVER the one at i+1 (Artin: x_i -> x_i x_{i+1} x_i^-1)
convention.why_it_is_safe: the Borromean control runs under the SAME convention, so a convention flip surfaces as a failed control rather than as silent zeros
convention.branches: both resolutions of the 2A+1 superposition letters are computed; lk is branch-dependent, so the Delta classes differ per branch

what_this_does_NOT_establish.milnor_in_general: NOT that Milnor invariants vanish generally -- the Borromean control in this file is a counterexample
what_this_does_NOT_establish.longer_invariants: length > 3 Milnor invariants are NOT examined
what_this_does_NOT_establish.route_2: untouched; blocked for an unrelated reason (Borromean-only genus handle)
what_this_does_NOT_establish.scope: (a), on the carrier as given at these isotopes in these two branches
